questions.stem: A patient with COPD presented with ARDS symptoms. What is the role of IL-8 in inflammation?
questions.solutionHtml:
Recruitment of neutrophils
  • In Acute lung injury after endothelial activation, alveolar macrophages releases pro-inflammatory mediators including IL 8 causing recruitment of neutrophils.


Robbins & Cotran Pathologic Basis of Disease, 10th Edition, Page No. 676

questions.stem: A patient presented with abdominal pain, hepatosplenomegaly and WBC count 50,000/mm3. Which of the following genes is involved in this case?
questions.solutionHtml:
t (9:22)
  • Presence of hepatosplenomegaly along with presence of marked leucocytosis, most probably is case of chronic myeloid leukemia, which have t (9:22)


Robbins & Cotran Pathologic Basis of Disease, 10th Edition, Page No. 622

questions.stem: A 55-year-old chronic smoker presents with weight loss, hemoptysis and a mass in the lung. Histopathological examination shows a tumor and IHC was performed for TTF-1 and shows positive expression. What is the possible diagnosis?
questions.solutionHtml:
Adenocarcinoma
  • Chronic smoker having history of weight loss, hemoptysis and presence of mass in lung, revealing positive expression of TTF 1 in tumor cells is suggestive of adenocarcinoma of lung


Robbins & Cotran Pathologic Basis of Disease, 10th Edition, Page No. 715-722

questions.stemHtml: A patient presents with flank pain and hematuria. The histology slide of the patient is provided. Based on the clinical presentation and histological findings, which of the following conditions is most likely?
questions.solutionHtml:
Chromophobe Renal Cell Carcinoma
  • Presence of flank pain and hematuria, histopathological examination showing prominent cell membranes, eosinophilic cytoplasm and perinuclear halo is characteristic of chromophobe renal cell carcinoma.


Robbins & Cotran Pathologic Basis of Disease, 10th Edition, Page No. 950

questions.stemHtml: A patient came to the OPD with complaints of vomiting and diarrhoea along with skin eruptions. He gives the history of similar episodes in the past. After switching to a gluten free diet his symptoms resolved. Which marker is useful in diagnosing this condition?
questions.solutionHtml:
Anti tissue transglutaminase antibody
  • In a patient switching to gluten free diet, symptoms of diarrhoea and vomiting resolved is suggestive of celiac disease.
  • Important diagnostic tests includes IgA tissue transglutaminase (tTG), IgA and IgG deaminated gliadin peptide (DGP)


Robbins & Cotran Pathologic Basis of Disease, 10th Edition, Page No. 784

questions.stemHtml: A 2 day old child is brought to the OPD. Mother complains that the child is not feeding well and has bilious vomiting. The child is diagnosed with congenital megacolon and aganglionic segment of the colon is shown. Which of the following layers are affected in this condition?
questions.solutionHtml:
Layer 2 and 3

Hirschsprung Disease (Congenital Aganglionic MegacolonQ)

  • Normal migration of neural crest cells from cecum to rectum is arrested prematurely
  • Distal intestinal segment lacks both the Meissner's submucosal and the Auerbach myenteric plexus.Q
  • Proximal to aganglionic segment, colon undergoes pro- gressive dilation
  • Defect always begins at the rectumQ, but extends proximally for variable lengths.
  • Aganglionic region may have a grossly normal or contracted appearance.Q
  • In contrast, the normally innervated proximal colon may undergo progressive dilation (megacolon)Q
  • Heterozygous loss of function mutations in RET gene causes most of familial cases & 15% of sporadic casesQ

Histology- Diagnosis of Hirschsprung disease requires histologic confirmation that ganglion cells are absent within the affected segment

  • Complete absence of submucosal and myenteric ganglion cells
  • Submucosal and myenteric nerve hypertrophy in aganglionic segment


Robbins & Cotran Pathologic Basis of Disease, 10th Edition, Page No.755

questions.stem: A COPD patient with a history of smoking presents with respiratory symptoms. High resolution CT showed panacinar emphysema. Which enzyme deficiency is associated with this condition?
questions.solutionHtml:
Alpha-1 antitrypsin
  • Panacinar type of emphysema is associated with deficiency of alpha 1 antitrypsin.


Robbins & Cotran Pathologic Basis of Disease, 10th Edition, Page No.679

questions.stemHtml: A 34-year-old female presented with low Hb, platelet count of 25000/mm3, raised PT and aPTT. A peripheral smear is given. Which of the following fusion genes is affected?
questions.solutionHtml:
PML RARA
  • Peripheral smear examination of 34 year old female shows Myleoblast with bundle of auer rod called a faggot cells seen in APML, predominantly showing t (15;17) PML RARA translocation.
  • Associated findings such as low platelet counts, increased PT and APTT also support the diagnosis of acute promyelocytic leukemia


Robbins & Cotran Pathologic Basis of Disease, 10th Edition, Page No. 617-620

questions.stemHtml: A 12-year-old child comes with cervical lymphadenopathy. Lymph node biopsy shows CD 10+, CD 19+, CD 20+, CD 5-, CD 23-, and Tdt -. What is the diagnosis?
questions.solutionHtml:
Burkitt lymphoma
  • Histopathological image from cervical lymph node shows medium-sized lymphoid cells having having high N:C ratio and conspicuous nucleoli along with multiple, small, round lipoid (clear) vacuoles in the cytoplasm, is suggestive of burkitt lymphoma as immunohistochemistry CD 10, CD 19 and CD 20 positivity also support the diagnosis.


Robbins & Cotran Pathologic Basis of Disease, 10th Edition, Page No. 601

questions.stemHtml: Identify the disease with the chromosomal abnormality?
questions.solutionHtml:
Prader Willi syndrome
  • Deletion or inactivation of paternal allele on chromosome 15q13 leading to maternal disomy is seen in prader Willi syndrome


Robbins & Cotran Pathologic Basis of Disease, 10th Edition, Page No. 178

questions.stem: A 49-year-old patient comes with complaints of left flank pain, hematuria, weight loss, headache, nausea, and convulsions. A family history of brain tumours and kidney tumours is present. MRI showed a cerebellar mass. What is the diagnosis?
questions.solutionHtml:
Von Hippel-Lindau syndrome
  • Presence of left flank with hematuria and familial history of brain tumor and renal tumors suggestive of familial renal cell carcinoma associated with VHL gene mutation. VHL patients develops cerebellar hemangioblastoma, Clear cell renal cell carcinoma and cysts in various organ


Robbins & Cotran Pathologic Basis of Disease, 10th Edition, Page No.949

questions.stemHtml: Which of the following is the most common mutation associated with the microscopy image of the thyroid shown?
questions.solutionHtml:
BRAF V600E
  • Histopathological image shows vague papillae formation, however shows presence of nuclear groove is suggestive of papillary carcinoma of thyroid and shows most commonly mutation in BRAF V600E


Robbins & Cotran Pathologic Basis of Disease, 10th Edition, Page No.1085

questions.stemHtml: Which condition is inherited according to the given pedigree?
questions.solutionHtml:
Wiskott-Aldrich Syndrome
  • Above pedigree shows female is a carrier and transmitting the disease to all offsprings, which will be manifested in male (as having single X chromosome) and carrier in female. Affected male does not transmit the disorder to his sons.


Robbins & Cotran Pathologic Basis of Disease, 10th Edition, Page No.146

questions.stem: Which of the following is not true about vWD?

options.label: A
options.text: VWD type 3 has severely low levels of VWF

options.label: B
options.text: VWD type 1 is the most severe disease in children

options.label: C
options.text: VWD type 3 is the most severe disease in children

options.label: D
options.text: VWD type 2 is associated with moderate bleeding tendency

questions.answerText: VWD type 1 is the most severe disease in children
questions.solutionHtml:
VWD type 1 is the most severe disease in children
  • Type 3 vWD (in children or in adults) have severe deficiency of von Willebrand Factor, hence will have severe vWD. Type 2 have qualitative vWF defects, will have moderate bleeding. Type 1 vWD is not presents with most severe disease


Robbins & Cotran Pathologic Basis of Disease, 10th Edition, Page No. 668

questions.stem: A 6-month-old child presented with leucocoria (cat's eye reflex) in the right eye. A cranial pathology was detected. The lesion is positive for synaptophysin, NSE, and chromogranin, and shows a palisade in a spoke-and- wheel arrangement, surrounding a central core. Identify the condition:NSE-Neuron specific enolase
questions.solutionHtml:
Retinoblastoma
  • A 6 month old baby with leucocoria (cat's eye reflex) in the right eye, is suggestive of retinoblastoma, which on IHC shows positivity for synaptophysin, chromogranine, and NSE


Robbins & Cotran Pathologic Basis of Disease, 10th Edition, Page No. 1324

questions.stemHtml: A 72-year-old man came with generalised anascarca and icterus. He had hepatosplenomegaly. Kidney function tests were found to be deranged and his urine gamma globulins were more than 3gm/dl. Electrophoresis of the urine protein is shown below. Which is the most likely diagnosis? RFT-Renal Function TestsSEP-Serum Protein Electrophoresis
questions.solutionHtml:
Multiple Myeloma – IgM
  • Urine electrophoresis shows presence of M spike along with deranged kidney function test, and gamma globulins of 3gm/dl is suggestive of multiple myeloma.


Robbins & Cotran Pathologic Basis of Disease, 10th Edition, Page No. 607

questions.stemHtml: A 10-year-old boy comes with visual disturbances and a headache. On imaging, he was found to have a suprasellar lesion. On biopsy and examination, the tumour exuded "black motor oil" like fluid. The MRI image is shown below. What is your likely diagnosis?
questions.solutionHtml:
Craniopharyngioma
  • Suprasellar lesion in 10 year old boy associated with visual disturbances and a headache with cystic configuration on taking biopsy is suggestive of craniopharyngioma


Robbins & Cotran Pathologic Basis of Disease, 10th Edition, Page No. 1074

questions.stem: Which among the following statements is true regarding PNH? PNH-Paroxysmal nocturnal hemoglobinuria

options.label: A
options.text: Anemia with heart failure is the most common cause of mortality

options.label: D
options.text: Flow cytometry is the gold standard for diagnosis

questions.answerText: Flow cytometry is the gold standard for diagnosis
questions.solutionHtml:
Flow cytometry is the gold standard for diagnosis
  • PNH has acquired defects in stem cells and the gold standard test is flow cytometry.


Robbins & Cotran Pathologic Basis of Disease, 10th Edition, Page No. 648

questions.stem: Which of the following is incorrect about iron metabolism?

options.label: A
options.text: Free serum iron is toxic to cells

options.label: B
options.text: Iron is stored in the body in the form of ferritin

options.label: C
options.text: Serum ferritin denotes the iron levels in the body

options.label: D
options.text: Iron is transported by binding with apoferritin

questions.answerText: Iron is transported by binding with apoferritin
questions.solutionHtml:
Iron is transported by binding with apoferritin
  • Iron absorbed from enterocytes is transferred to a plasma protein transferrin that delivers it to different cells. Rest of the statements are true.


Robbins & Cotran Pathologic Basis of Disease, 10th Edition, Page No. 655

questions.stemHtml: A 45 year old woman came with complaints of fever, night sweats, generalised itching and unintentional weight loss of 10% in the last 3 months. On examination, she has enlarged cervical and axillary lymph nodes. The lymph node examination and biopsy showed the following picture. What would the likely diagnosis and treatment option be?

options.label: B
options.text: Non Hodgkin's Lymphoma – Poor prognosis due to advanced stage - treated with radiotherapy

questions.solutionHtml:
Hodgkin's Lymphoma – ABVD regimen
  • A 45 Year old female with cervical lymphadenopathy which on biopsy for binucleate cells having owl eye appearance (Reed-sternberg cells) is suggestive of Hodgkin’s lymphoma and usually regime given is ABVD


Robbins & Cotran Pathologic Basis of Disease, 10th Edition, Page No. 611

questions.stemHtml: A 53-year-old woman came with complaints of fatigue, nausea, anasarca and proteinuria. She had anaemia and neutropenia. Her Bone marrow examination showed 22% plasma cells and acellular eosinophilic deposits. The bone marrow biopsy is shown below. What is the associated pathology?

options.label: D
options.text: Myxomatous degeneration of the bone marrow

questions.solutionHtml:
Amyloidosis
  • Presence of 22% plasma cells in bone marrow is suggestive of diagnosis of multiple myeloma, it is associate with amyloid deposition, which is seen as amorphous acellular eosinophilic material deposition, seen in above image


Robbins & Cotran Pathologic Basis of Disease, 10th Edition, Page No. 648

questions.stem: A patient presented with an arm span of more than height, a subluxated lens, and a pigeon chest appearance. What is the likely protein involved in this condition?
questions.solutionHtml:
Fibrillin
  • Having long arms, pigeon chest and subluxated lens is suggestive of Marfan syndrome and it is an autosomal dominant disease having mutation in the fibrillin gene on chromosome 15q21


Robbins & Cotran Pathologic Basis of Disease, 10th Edition, Page No. 148

questions.stem: Which method is more effective than measuring clotting factors for assessing the intrinsic pathway of coagulation?PT-Prothrombin timeAPTT-Activated partial thromboplastin timeCBC-Complete blood count
questions.solutionHtml:
APTT

APTT is used to detect functioning of clotting factors in intrinsic pathway



Robbins & Cotran Pathologic Basis of Disease, 10th Edition, Page No. 663

questions.stemHtml: A 38-year-old woman came with complaints of a slowly growing breast lump for the last 6 months. She had a history of a similar lump for which excision was done and medical and mammographic reports are not available. On examination, the lump was smooth, well-defined, mobile and with regular margins. The cytology and biopsy of the same were taken and are shown below. What is the most likely diagnosis?
questions.solutionHtml:
Phyllodes tumor

● A 48 year old female having breast lump since 6 months which is smooth and mobile, histology shows leaf like protrusion and proliferating stroma covered by epithelium and occasional protrusion into cystic spaces, suggestive of phyllodes tumor.



Robbins & Cotran Pathologic Basis of Disease, 10th Edition, Page No. 1062

questions.stemHtml: A middle aged man came with complaints of dyspnea, chest tightness and dry cough. On imaging, he was found to have diffuse interstitial fibrosis. The biopsy of his lung was taken and is shown below. Which of the following industries he has likely been working in for the last 20 years?
questions.solutionHtml:
Asbestos

An industry worker for 20 years having complaints of dyspnea, chest tightness and dry cough and histopathologic image showing asbestos bodies is suggestive of asbestosis



Robbins & Cotran Pathologic Basis of Disease, 10th Edition, Page No. 691

questions.stemHtml: An adult male presented with protruding abdomen, diarrhoea, visual symptoms and neurological manifestations. Based on the peripheral smear finding. What is the likely diagnosis?
questions.solutionHtml:
Abetalipoproteinemia
  • Peripheral smear showing circumferential spiky projections on the RBC( burr cells) associated with visual and neurological symptoms is suggestive abetalipoproteinemia.


Robbins & Cotran Pathologic Basis of Disease, 10th Edition, Page No. 674

questions.stemHtml: A patient passed away following a myocardial infarction. An autopsy was conducted and the biopsy findings of his cardiac tissue are shown below. What is the number of days since the injury, based on the given findings?
questions.solutionHtml:
1 day
  • Patient died of MI autopsy conducted and biopsy from cardiac tissue shows presence of neutrophils is suggestive of lesion of 1-2 days.


Robbins & Cotran Pathologic Basis of Disease, 10th Edition, Page No. 543

questions.stemHtml: A 45 year old man came with complaints of tearing chest pain, tachycardia, and hypotension with negative Trop I and T. The wall of the aorta was biopsied and the image is shown below. What is the most likely pathology behind it?

options.label: A
options.text: Connective tissue damage of the aortic wall

options.label: B
options.text: Fibrinoid necrosis and smooth muscle hyperplasia

options.label: C
options.text: Fat deposition and smooth muscle degeneration

questions.answerText: Connective tissue damage of the aortic wall
questions.solutionHtml:
Connective tissue damage of the aortic wall

Histopathological image of a patient shows splitting of aortic wall, associated with chest pain and tachycardia is suggestive of aortic dissection



Robbins & Cotran Pathologic Basis of Disease, 10th Edition, Page No. 507

questions.stem: Which protein accumulation is seen in Alzheimer's disease?GFAP-Glial fibrillary acidic protein
questions.solutionHtml:
Aẞ Amyloid
  • The fundamental abnormality in AD is the accumulation of two proteins (Aβ and tau) in specific brain regions, likely as a result of excessive production and defective removal.


Robbins & Cotran Pathologic Basis of Disease, 10th Edition, Page No. 1275

questions.stem: A couple comes for prenatal genetic counselling. They have a family history of Hemophilia. They have a male child with Hemophilia and a normal female child. The mother's family has Hemophilia and the father's family is normal. What are the chances of their offspring being affected?

options.label: A
options.text: All males will be affected and all females 7.7% will be normal

options.label: B
options.text: Half of the males can be affected and 61.3% half of the females can be carriers

options.label: C
options.text: All males will be affected and half of the 30.58% females will be carriers

options.label: D
options.text: All of males and females will be affected

questions.answerText: Half of the males can be affected and 61.3% half of the females can be carriers
questions.solutionHtml:
Half of the males can be affected and 61.3% half of the females can be carriers

Hemophilia is X linked recessive  inherited disorder, hence male can transmits disease to male and recessive X to female (carrier)



Robbins & Cotran Pathologic Basis of Disease, 10th Edition, Page No. 146

questions.stemHtml: A 10-year-old boy comes with a fever and pain in his right upper limb. He has an expansile lesion in his right radius in the diaphysis. The histopathology of the lesion is shown below. What is the most accurate test among the following?
questions.solutionHtml:
EWSR1 (FUS-ETS fusion gene)
  • Histopathological image from bony lesion shows features of small round cell tumor having monomorphic tumor cells having high N:C ratio, round to oval nuclei and conspicuous nucleoli, associated with fever and pain is diagnostic of Ewings sarcoma having EWSR1 (FUS-ETS fusion gene)


Robbins & Cotran Pathologic Basis of Disease, 10th Edition, Page No. 1192

questions.stem: A 28 year old woman P1L1, came with complaints of weakness and generalised fatigue. The peripheral blood picture showed microcytic hypochromic anemia. Her serum iron was low and she had increased RDW. Her MCV and MCH were also low and TIBC was high. What would her serum transferrin saturation be?MCV-Mean corpuscular volumeMCH-Mean corpuscular hemoglobinTIBC-Total iron-binding capacity
questions.solutionHtml:
Reduced
  • Peripheral blood morphology of microcytic hypochromic anemia, along with low iron, MCV and MCHC and high TIBC suggestive iron deficiency anemia, and her serum transferrin saturation will be low as iron store is less.


Robbins & Cotran Pathologic Basis of Disease, 10th Edition, Page No. 655

questions.stemHtml: A 38-year-old woman came with complaints of weakness, lethargy, and heavy menstrual bleeding. Her peripheral blood picture showed small RBCs with pallor. Lab investigations are given below. What is the diagnosis?
questions.solutionHtml:
Iron-Deficiency Anemia
  • Lab investigations showing low Hb, along with low MCV, MCH and transferrin saturation associated with high TBC in 38 year old females having Hb of 7.9 mg/dl is suggestive of iron deficiency anemia.


Robbins & Cotran Pathologic Basis of Disease, 10th Edition, Page No. 655
